Comment: Economy tables: the five acts (gated by net worth and reputation, never a quest flag), wages by role, prices and the demand elasticities. Money is USD at 2020s European/North American resort levels. Act thresholds sit above the net worth a resort holds at the start of each act (Act I: a T-bar and an old cat, about 0.7 M; Act II: the Silberhorn fixed-grip quad, about 4 M), so every act is earned by a season or two of operating profit. Loan ceilings follow lift capex: a detachable quad is about 9 M for 1 km, a 3S across the gorge 50-60 M.

Acts.Comment: One T-bar, one green run, a tired groomer. Surface lifts and fixed-grip doubles only; the bank offers a 150 k overdraft. A village hill charges under 40 USD and draws about 200 skiers on a weekday.
Fixed-grip quads and triples, a pulse gondola, tier-2 machines, first hires. Reached with 1 M of net worth and an average reputation.
Snowmaking, road and lot maintenance, tier-3 machines; detachable quads and 8-passenger gondolas become buildable. 5 M net worth is the quad plus a season of profit.

Six-packs, 10-passenger gondolas, chondolas, trams and funiculars, tier-4 fleet. The loan ceiling covers a detachable line whose extra capacity wears the piste faster than the extra tickets pay for grooming.
Everything: funitel, bicable and tricable gondolas, the 150-passenger tram, eight-packs, tier-5 machines. Destination pricing above 100 USD and four-thousand-skier weekdays.

Wages.Comment: Lift attendant/operator, seasonal hourly; posted per operating hour per StaffRequired head.
Night-shift snowcat operator with a groomer licence; nine-hour shift including the walk-around.
Heavy-equipment mechanic; charged per workshop hour on PM, repair and rebuild jobs.
Ski patrol with avalanche and rescue training.
Ski school instructor, paid per teaching hour.
Construction crew hand on lift and run projects; matches construction.json LaborRatePerHour.
